speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and weakness in your upper limbs; to better understand the nature of your condition, could you tell me if these symptoms have been getting worse over the last few weeks or months?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of worsening weakness with rest and double vision upon looking up or down are highly suggestive of a specific neuromuscular condition. To confirm this, I need to see if you experience a diplopia that reverses when you cover one eye, and REQUEST TEST: Routine_Blood_Work (including CK levels).

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The symptom pattern of fatigue with activity and improvement with rest, combined with specific diplopia on vertical gaze, is classic for this neuromuscular junction disorder; the suggestion of Tuberculosis is clinically inconsistent with these findings.
